text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- An International Monetary Fund mission arrived in Sofia to discuss the introduction of a currency board system in Bulgaria.

-- Bulgarian customs officials said they had seized 10 kg of hashish worth some $1 million and hidden in a Mercedes car with Albanian registration arriving from Turkey at the Bulgarian-Turkish border checkpoint Kapitan Andreevo. @
-- Bulgaria's Chief Prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev said he had received anonymous phone threats and additional security measures had been taken to protect his life as a result.
-- The Sofia City court is expected to rule on an insolvency claim against Bulgaria's First Private bank filed by the central bank by the year's end, court officials said. @

-- Bulgaria's opposition deputy Ventseslav Dimitrov said he had proposed to the parliamentary budget committee a draft decision to approve a five-year rescheduling of payments on Bulgaria's domestic debt in a bid to secure payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt.

-- Employees at Bulgaria's state magnetic storage device producer DZU-Stara Zagora approached the cabinet to buy a 20 percent stake in the company and the other 80 percent might be offered to a foreign investor, a DZU senior official said. @

-- Bulgaria is in talks with Japan for some $600 million credit to Bulgaria's National Electric Company for the construction of a new coal-fired power plant in Bulgaria's power complex Maritsa East One, Energy minister Roumen Ovcharov said.
-- Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by 171 billion levs to 839 billion levs in November or around 50 percent of Bulgaria's gross domestic product, Finance ministry figures showed. @
-- Bulgaria has completed the autumn sowing of 1.5 million hectares of wheat and barley, nearly meeting the target of 1.6 million ha, an Agriculture ministry officuial said.

-- Bulgaria had agreed supplies of Russian nuclear fuel with payments to be secured by selling electricity to Bulgaria's Balkan neighbours, Energy minister Roumen Ovcharov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
